title: ICT dynamics for gender inclusive intermediary education: minimum poverty and inequality thresholds in developing countries
decision_rationale: Own system-GMM estimation of ICT indicators on gender parity in school enrolment (family 5) in 57 developing countries; exposure and sample criteria met.
exposure_measure: Six indicators: internet access in schools (GITR index), use of virtual social networks (GITR index), internet users per 100, fixed broadband per 100, % persons with PC, mobile subscriptions per 100; interacted with Gini, Atkinson, Palma ratio, poverty headcount (national lines)

sample.economies_or_groups: 57 developing countries (Table 2 list), Asia, Africa, Latin America, E. Europe
sample.income_groups_covered: mixed (low and middle income; text says 'developing'; no per-group split, Table 2 income levels not shown in text)

design.estimator: Interactive system GMM (Roodman-type, lagged dependent variable), 33 instruments
design.key_controls_fixed_effects: Lagged DV, remittances/GDP, time effects; inequality or poverty term and ICT x inequality interaction

results.indicator: Gender parity index, gross primary+secondary enrolment; internet access in school
results.estimate: Table 4 col1 (Gini): ICT 0.0309; Gini x ICT -0.0550; threshold 0.5618; poverty col4: ICT 0.0128, Poverty x ICT -0.00038, threshold 33.6842; Atkinson col: ICT -0.0190
results.uncertainty: p=0.002 (Gini col); p=0.000 (poverty col); p=0.000 (Atkinson col, marked **)
results.evidence: Table 4, p.13: 'ICT in school 0.0309 (0.002)***'; 'Gini x ICTschool -0.0550 (0.007)***'

results.indicator: GPI; use of virtual social network
results.evidence: Table 4, p.13; Palma threshold 9.1153 lies outside sample range (max 8.4098, p.12)
Table 5, p.14; only Palma col significant, threshold 3.3766

heterogeneity.finding: Inequality (Gini, Palma) and poverty dampen ICT effect on gender parity; interaction mostly negative for school internet, computers; critical thresholds reported

n_specifications_reported: 48 (6 ICT x 4 inequality/poverty measures x 2 tables of 8... ie 6 x 4 = 24 regressions)

confounding_reverse_causation.why: Causal language and thresholds; only internal GMM instruments, few controls (remittances only), Sargan rejects in several columns, AR(1) p near 0.09

exposure_measurement.why: Mixed survey-index (GITR) and WDI measures; PC variable and school internet are weak proxies; text describes Table 3 label inconsistently

selection_of_countries_years.why: Only 5 years (2012-2016), unbalanced, 57 countries chosen by data availability; N=285 with 33 instruments

outcome_measurement.why: Gross enrolment GPI measures parity not quality; values above 1 possible

specification_and_researcher_degrees_of_.why: 24 ICT x moderator specifications, thresholds computed only where signs fit hypotheses; Fisher stats huge, near-unit-root lagged DV coefficients (up to 1.005)

selective_reporting.why: Thresholds reported only for hypotheses-consistent columns; text says models 'valid overwhelmingly' though Sargan p<0.05 in many; abstract highlights favourable results

venue_quality_concern: possible (working paper version of single-author-network research with templated design; threshold computed from point estimates without uncertainty)
notes: Poverty/inequality are moderators, not outcomes; outcome is family 5 (schooling parity). Table 3 notes mislabel PALM as poverty headcount and POV blank; Table 2 referred to as summary stats and correlation numbering inconsistent. Table 4 Palma threshold 9.1153 exceeds sample max and abstract does not claim it. Some stars in Table 4 inconsistent with printed p. No instructions embedded in text.
